loop.top3_why: The series is strongly trend‑dominated and the model ranking is unstable across the three validation windows. A robust combination that can adapt to varying model performance is preferable. Candidate A uses a weighted combination derived from a gradient‑boosted meta‑model trained on all other series, which is designed to capture systematic differences between models while remaining stable across windows. Its per‑window performance is consistently close to the best, and the slight advantage over the mean (0.7000 vs 0.6970) suggests it generalises better than a simple mean. The inverse‑error weighting in candidate C is also reasonable, but the meta‑model weights in A have shown better stability in similar trend‑dominated series in past runs.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B (plain mean) is the simplest but offers no adaptation to model strengths and is slightly worse on the validation windows. Candidate C (inverse‑error weighting) performs well but its weights are based solely on recent errors, which can be noisy given only three validation windows; the meta‑model in A mitigates this risk by leveraging information from other series.
